feedback.problem: The coefficient of ${b}^{4}$ in the expansion of ${(1-\frac{b}{3})}^{9}$ is
feedback.worked_solution:
The binomial expansion for $(1+x)^{n}$ is given by

$$
(1+x)^{n}=1+nx+\frac{n(n-1)}{2!}{x}^{2}+⋯.
$$

In particular, the ${x}^{4}$ term is given by

$$
\frac{n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)}{4!}{x}^{4}.
$$

Replacing $x$ with $-\frac{b}{3}$ and $n$ with $9$ in the above expression, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{9(9-1)(9-2)(9-3)}{4!}\cdot {(-\frac{b}{3})}^{4} & =\frac{9\cdot 8\cdot 7\cdot 6}{24}\cdot {(-\frac{1}{3})}^{4}\cdot {b}^{4} \\  & =126\cdot \frac{1}{81}{b}^{4} \\  & =\frac{14}{9}{b}^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coefficient of ${b}^{4}$ is $\frac{14}{9}.$
